messages.subject: Re: ddply rescaler inside a function
messages.body_plain:
> Ok, the following are completely guessing.
> The problem seems to be that rescaler is only looking for sctype in
> the data frame and global environment, not the "local environment" for
> the function. Probably because the transform function did not pass
> that local environment to rescaler?

I think the problem is with transform, not with rescaler.  If you look
at the source code to transform, you'll see it's evaluating in the
context of parent.frame().  Because transform is activated inside
llply, the parent.frame points to the wrong place and it can't find
sctype.  I think the correct way to fix this is to evaluate in the
function in the parent.frame of ddply, but this will take quite a bit
of rewiring.  I've added it to my to do list
(http://github.com/hadley/plyr/issues/issue/3), but it might be a
while before I can get around to implementing it

Hadley

--

Department of Statistics / Rice University

messages.subject: as.quoted with names with spaces
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

The plyr package currently does not handle variable names with spaces
in them:

> df <- data.frame(x = c(1,2,3))
> df$"Column Name" <- c(4,5,6)
> df
  x Column Name
1 1           4
2 2           5
3 3           6
> ddply(df, .variable=c("x"), sum)
  x V1
1 1  5
2 2  7
3 3  9
> ddply(df, .variable=c("Column Name"), sum)
Error in parse(text = x) : unexpected symbol in "Column Name"

Is this a bug that can be fixed?

Short of renaming columns is there anything that can be used a
preprocessing step or as a workaround?

Thanks,
Matt

messages.subject: Re: apparent Date bug in plyr 0.1.9
messages.body_plain:
FYI, yes, it was rv that was doing weird things with generics so that 1 + rvobject and c(1, rvobject) will work. I've given up on the rv package and rewrote (some of) it using proto objects. I lose all of the nice operator overloading, so I have to write rvobj1$plus(rvobj2) or rvobject$c(1), but at least it doesn't break anything!

I'm likely to rewrite rv in Scala too. Looking forward to implicit conversions  <http://paulbarry.com/articles/2009/04/17/implicit-conversions-scalas-type-safe-answer-to-rubys-open-class>to solve this problem!

 -Harlan

>
>  -Harlan
>
>

> > >> ddply(dd, .(x), function(q) {q})
> > > Error in NextMethod(.Generic) : no method to invoke
> > >
> > > How could rv break plyr if it's not masking any of plyr's objects?
> >
> > Maybe it's creating a new generic that conflicts with some functions
> > in plyr?  I dunno.
> >
> > Hadley
